subtitle: How Buddhist Thinkers Forged a Science of Knowing

panels.shot: epic split composition, half ancient debate hall, half mountain monastery overlooking vast plains
panels.action: Dignaga & Dharmakirti stand back-to-back, scrolls and palm-leaf manuscripts in hand, as shadowy figures of debaters gather around them in a timeless scholastic space stretching from India toward the Himalaya.

dialogue.text: In an age of fierce argument, Dignaga and Dharmakirti dared a dangerous question: what counts as real proof?

i18n.hi: कड़े विवाद के युग में, दिग्नाग और धर्मकीर्ति ने खतरनाक सवाल उठाया: असली प्रमाण क्या है?

panels.shot: wide interior shot of a bustling monastic hall in South Asia, low angle
panels.action: Young monks and brahmin scholars face each other in a crowded assembly hall; Dignaga & Dharmakirti are shown smaller among them, listening intently as elders debate under hanging oil lamps.

dialogue.text: Across South Asia in the fifth and seventh centuries, halls like these rang with debate: Buddhists, Nyaya logicians, Mimamsa ritualists, all fighting with reasons instead of swords.

i18n.hi: पाँचवीं से सातवीं सदी में, ऐसे सभागार बहस से गूंजते थे: बौद्ध, न्याय तर्कशास्त्री, मीमांसा कर्मकांडी—सब तलवारें नहीं, तर्कों से लड़ते थे।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Dignaga’s focused face, three-quarter profile
panels.action: Dignaga, depicted as a middle-aged monk-scholar, sits cross-legged on a simple mat, eyes narrowed, listening to a Nyaya teacher sketch a complex argument with a stick on the floor.

dialogue.text: Dignaga hears learned men invoke scriptures, grammar, tradition, even dreams as sources of knowledge. He wonders: can a Buddhist path rest on such shifting sands?

i18n.hi: दिग्नाग विद्वानों को सुनता है—शास्त्र, व्याकरण, परंपरा, सपने तक ज्ञान के स्रोत कहे जा रहे हैं। वह सोचता है: क्या बौद्ध मार्ग इतनी डगमग नींव पर टिक सकता है?

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder close-up on Dignaga’s hand writing on a palm-leaf manuscript
panels.action: By a small window, Dignaga leans over palm leaves, carefully inscribing neat characters, a single oil lamp illuminating his concentrated face and the black-ink lines.

dialogue.text: In his Pramana-samuccaya, Dignaga makes a stark move: he calls only two things ‘valid means of knowledge’—direct perception and inference built from it.

i18n.hi: अपने ‘प्रमाणसमुच्चय’ में दिग्नाग कठोर कदम उठाता है: वह सिर्फ दो चीजों को ‘सच्चा ज्ञान-साधन’ मानता है—सीधा प्रत्यक्ष और उससे बना अनुमान।

panels.shot: conceptual wide shot, half realist half symbolic
panels.action: On one side, Dignaga touches a bright lotus to his eyes; on the other, logical diagrams seem to rise as glowing lines between objects, monks, and the lotus, symbolizing perception and inference.

dialogue.text: Perception, he writes, grasps the particular as it appears. Inference, built from patterns of cause and effect, reaches what perception cannot see.

i18n.hi: वह लिखता है, प्रत्यक्ष जैसा दिखे वैसा ही खास रूप पकड़ता है। कारण–फल के ठोस ढाँचों से बना अनुमान वहाँ पहुँचता है जहाँ आँखें नहीं पहुँचतीं।

panels.shot: tense medium shot of small debate circle, eye level
panels.action: Dignaga sits opposite a Nyaya scholar in an open courtyard, both surrounded by a circle of attentive students; the Nyaya scholar gestures toward stacked manuscripts as he argues.

dialogue.speaker: Nyaya scholar
dialogue.text: You Buddhists cut away too much. Scripture and testimony are pramana as well!

i18n.hi: तुम बौद्ध तो बहुत कुछ काट फेंकते हो। शास्त्र और वचन भी तो प्रमाण हैं!

panels.shot: calm close-up on Dignaga, slightly low angle
panels.action: Dignaga raises one hand gently, expression calm but firm, while distant stupas and temple spires rise behind him, hinting at the wider world his words will reach.

dialogue.text: Dignaga answers that testimony and scripture matter, but only as inference: we trust a word when perception and reasoning show its speaker to be reliable.

i18n.hi: दिग्नाग कहता है, वचन और शास्त्र ज़रूरी हैं, पर केवल अनुमान की तरह: हम उसी बात पर भरोसा करते हैं, जिसके कहने वाले की विश्वसनीयता प्रत्यक्ष और तर्क से साबित हो।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide shot of manuscript being copied by many hands
panels.action: Rows of monks copy Dignaga’s text; the image suggests passing years as palm-leaf manuscripts travel by caravan, boat, and foot from one monastery to another.

dialogue.text: His careful arguments spread through Buddhist scholastic networks. In India and beyond, they reshape how monks trained in logic frame every debate.

i18n.hi: उसकी तर्क-रेखाएँ बौद्ध विद्या-जालों में फैल जाती हैं। भारत और बाहर, वे हर बहस की बौद्धिक ट्रेनिंग की भाषा बदल देती हैं।

panels.shot: transition shot, Dharmakirti entering a bustling monastic compound, three-quarter wide
panels.action: Dharmakirti, shown as a younger monk with sharp eyes, steps through the stone gateway of a large monastery; teachers and students cluster in courtyards lined with cells and lecture halls.

dialogue.text: A century later, Dharmakirti arrives in this world of organized study. He inherits Dignaga’s questions—and finds the enemies of Buddhism better armed than ever.

i18n.hi: एक सदी बाद धर्मकीर्ति इस संगठित अध्ययन की दुनिया में आता है। वह दिग्नाग के सवालों को सँभालता है—और देखता है कि बौद्ध धर्म के विरोधी पहले से ज़्यादा हथियारबंद हैं।

panels.shot: intense close-up on Dharmakirti’s eyes over an open Dignaga manuscript
panels.action: Dharmakirti sits alone in a cell, Dignaga’s work open before him, lips moving silently as he reads, while complex thought-diagrams glow faintly around his head like constellations.

dialogue.text: In his Pramana-varttika, he sharpens the tools. What is a cause? What makes an inference fail? How can compassion stand firm under hostile scrutiny?

i18n.hi: अपने ‘प्रमाणवर्त्तिक’ में वह औज़ार पैने करता है: कारण क्या है? अनुमान कब टूट जाता है? करुणा दुश्मन की कड़ी जाँच के सामने कैसे अडिग रहे?

panels.shot: medium shot of Dharmakirti teaching, chalking a logical pattern on a wall or board
panels.action: Dharmakirti stands before a small group of monks, sketching a three-part syllogism onto a smoothed clay wall, while students watch and count off the steps on their fingers.

dialogue.text: He insists that an inference must rest on unfailing connection: wherever there is smoke, there is fire. Loose examples, he warns, cannot support a path that claims to end suffering.

i18n.hi: वह ज़िद करता है कि अनुमान अटूट संबंध पर टिके: जहाँ धुआँ है, वहाँ आग है। ढीले मिसालें, वह चेताता है, उस मार्ग को नहीं थाम सकतीं जो दुःख का अंत दावा करता है।

panels.shot: dramatic debate-hall wide shot, two schools facing off
panels.action: Dharmakirti, flanked by Buddhist monks, stands opposite Nyaya and Mimamsa scholars in a formal debate hall; each side’s followers sit in disciplined rows behind their champion.

dialogue.text: Against Nyaya and Mimamsa, Dharmakirti wields this tightened logic like a discipline. His aim is not dominance, but to show that Buddhist claims can face the harshest tests.

i18n.hi: न्याय और मीमांसा के सामने धर्मकीर्ति इस कसकर बँधे तर्क को अनुशासन की तरह चलाता है। उसका लक्ष्य जीत नहीं, यह दिखाना है कि बौद्ध दावे सबसे कड़ी परीक्षा झेल सकते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up on Dharmakirti’s hand over his heart, side angle
panels.action: After a long session, Dharmakirti steps down from the debate platform, fingers resting over his chest, his face thoughtful rather than triumphant, as students approach with questions.

dialogue.speaker: Dharmakirti
dialogue.text: Reason must guard the Dharma, or we risk comforting words where truth is needed.

i18n.hi: तर्क को धर्म की रखवाली करनी होगी, वरना जहाँ सत्य चाहिए वहाँ हम सिर्फ दिलासा भरे शब्द दे बैठेंगे।

panels.shot: montage wide shot, Indian monastery dissolving into Tibetan mountain monastery
panels.action: The image blends an Indian monastic compound into a high Himalayan monastery; robed Tibetan monks sit in rows, chanting and debating, with texts of Dignaga and Dharmakirti before them.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, in Tibet, their works become pillars of training. Young monks memorize, debate, and rebuild these systems, making Buddhist logic a living practice far from its birthplace.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद तिब्बत में उनकी रचनाएँ प्रशिक्षण के स्तंभ बनती हैं। युवा भिक्षु इन्हें कंठस्थ करते, बहसते, फिर से गढ़ते हैं—जन्मभूमि से दूर बौद्ध तर्क को जीवित साधना बना देते हैं।

panels.shot: conceptual bird’s-eye shot over a vast network of monasteries connected by glowing lines
panels.action: From above, dozens of monasteries across South Asia and the Himalaya are shown, linked by faint, luminous paths; tiny figures debate under the same sun, with Dignaga and Dharmakirti faintly superimposed.

dialogue.text: Their ideas do not erase other Indian logics. Instead, they join a long, contested conversation on reason, proof, and what it means to claim knowledge at all.

i18n.hi: उनके विचार बाकी भारतीय तर्कों को मिटाते नहीं। वे तो एक लंबी, विवादित बातचीत में जुड़ते हैं—तर्क, प्रमाण, और ज्ञान का दावा करने के मायने पर।

panels.shot: quiet medium shot of a modern scholar in a study, parallel composition
panels.action: A present-day scholar sits at a desk surrounded by editions of Pramana-samuccaya and Pramana-varttika, tracing arguments on paper as a faint silhouette of Dignaga & Dharmakirti appears behind him.

dialogue.text: Modern researchers still parse their pages, seeing not myth but a disciplined attempt to build a science of knowing inside a world of faith.

i18n.hi: आज के शोधकर्ता भी उनकी पन्नियाँ खंगालते हैं—उन्हें मिथक नहीं, आस्था की दुनिया के भीतर ज्ञान की विज्ञान बनाने की अनुशासित कोशिश मानते हैं।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot, Dignaga and Dharmakirti seated facing a horizon
panels.action: Dignaga & Dharmakirti sit side by side on a hill at dusk, overlooking valleys dotted with monasteries and villages, their manuscripts resting quietly beside them.

dialogue.text: Their legacy is a simple demand with vast reach: if compassion is our goal, our thinking must be clear enough to be tested—and brave enough to be corrected.

i18n.hi: उनकी विरासत एक सीधी माँग में सिमटती है, जिसका दायरा विशाल है: अगर करुणा लक्ष्य है, तो सोच इतनी साफ हो कि जाँची जा सके—और इतनी साहसी कि सुधरने को तैयार रहे।
